newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sharply higher on cold, funds return.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sharply higher on cold, funds return.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures staged a stunning recovery on Friday, as traders' attention turned to colder weather and investment funds piled on new long positions, brokers said.
January Brent, which is due to expire on Monday, closed $1.03 up at $23.55 per barrel, while February Brent ended 76 cents higher at $22.91.

"Some people are talking about the cold weather factor, but we definitely saw some fund activity towards the close," a broker said. "It's a thin market, so if the funds need to come in and do some business, it pushes the market around."
Even after Friday's rally, January Brent ended the week 70 cents off Monday's high as Iraq's return to the oil market came closer to reality.

The official Turkish news agency said the first tanker of crude should load from the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan on Monday. In New York, the U.N. said on Thursday night it had approved five contracts to buy Iraqi oil.
IPE gas oil futures closed earlier $8.50 higher on the back of NYMEX gains built on forecasts of cold European and U.S. weather, traders said.
"It was a very strong, nice close, following (New York) heating up," a trader said. "It was a good move up, especially since the fundamentals in Europe don't look too clever."
January gas oil futures finished at $213.75, up from $212.00 in midafternoon. Much of the focus was on buying of the Jan/Feb spread, which grew $1.50 over the session to finish at $6.
Private forecasters WSC said western European temperatures would continue well below average for the time of year, and also saw below-average temeratures in the U.S. midwest next week.
